LESSON: NON- METALLIC MATERIALS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Materials for Production
Topic 3.3: Non- Metallic Materials
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Non- Metallic Materials, part of Materials for Production in Grade 7 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why are non-metallic materials important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify non-metallic materials found in the locality,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Non- Metallic Materials in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. categorise non-metallic materials as either synthetic or natural,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Non- Metallic Materials in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. describe the physical properties of non-metallic materials found in the locality,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Non- Metallic Materials in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. relate non-metallic materials to their uses in the locality,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Non- Metallic Materials in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate the use of non- metallic materials in production.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Non- Metallic Materials in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify non-metallic materials found in the locality,

   Non- Metallic Materials helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. categorise non-metallic materials as either synthetic or natural,

   Non- Metallic Materials helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. describe the physical properties of non-metallic materials found in the locality,

   Non- Metallic Materials helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. relate non-metallic materials to their uses in the locality,

   Non- Metallic Materials helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. appreciate the use of non- metallic materials in production.

   Non- Metallic Materials helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use print or digital media to search for information on non- metallic materials,

2. discuss the non-metallic materials (wood, stone, plastics, paper, rubber, cement, glass, ceramics),

3. sort non-metallic materials as either synthetic or natural,

4. perform practical activities to examine the physical properties of non-metallic materials (color, texture, hardness, fire resistance),

5. discuss the physical properties of non-metallic materials,

6. match non-metallic materials to their use in the locality.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use print or digital media to search for information on non- metallic materials,
2. discuss the non-metallic materials (wood, stone, plastics, paper, rubber, cement, glass, ceramics),
3. sort non-metallic materials as either synthetic or natural,
4. perform practical activities to examine the physical properties of non-metallic materials (color, texture, hardness, fire resistance),
5. discuss the physical properties of non-metallic materials,
6. match non-metallic materials to their use in the locality.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Non- Metallic Materials together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: learner develops evaluation and decision skills when sorting non-metallic materials

as either synthetic or natural.

• Creativity and Imagination: learner develops observation skills when performing practical activities to examine the physical

properties of non-metallic materials.

Values:
• Peace: learner displays respect for self and peers when discussing non-metallic materials.

• Unity: learner displays team spirit and collaboration with others when performing practical activities to examine the physical

properties of non-metallic materials.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCI’s):

Personal Safety and Security: learner observes safety precautions when performing practical activities to examine the physical

properties of non-metallic materials.

Link to other Subjects:

Integrated Science: learner enhances knowledge on use of matter during the matching of non- metallic materials to their use in

the locality.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify non-metallic materials found in the locality,
2. categorise non-metallic materials as either synthetic or natural,
3. describe the physical properties of non-metallic materials found in the locality,
4. relate non-metallic materials to their uses in the locality,
5. appreciate the use of non- metallic materials in production.

Remember the key question: Why are non-metallic materials important?
